# Volvo Cars storsatsar – Frontlines vd om oljan

**Feed**: efn-borsfrukost  
**Published**: 2026-09-17  
**Market Sentiment**: Mixed

⏱️ **Time Horizon Key**: ST = <3 months | MT = 3-12 months | LT = >12 months

---

## Episode Thesis

EFN Morgon discusses the Fed's expected 25bp hike under Kevin Warsh, which came with a hawkish tone but a stronger economic outlook. It also covers Volvo Cars' strategy day (8%+ EBIT margin target, 13 new models, deeper Geely ties) and an interview with Frontline's CEO on very high VLCC rates caused by the Iran conflict. Guest Per Hedberg is cutting bank exposure (JPMorgan, NatWest) and adding insurance, owns fertiliser and food input plays (CF Industries, ADM) as an oil-price hedge, and is cautious that AI capex growth is peaking and that the run-up to the US midterms usually brings a weak market.

---

## Universe Stocks

### 🟡 JPM — JPMorgan | **HOLD** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: MT  
**Confidence**: 70%

Guest's long-standing core bank holding, trimmed recently as the yield curve flattens.

#### Reasoning

Guest (Per Hedberg) calls JPMorgan the stable go-to bank that has handled every crisis well and is a core holding. He sold part of it because the long-short rate spread is narrowing after the Fed and the peak cyclical boost is fading, so he is rotating from banks into insurance. Still owned, so this is a hold with reduced weight.

#### Sell Triggers

- further yield curve flattening
- cyclical slowdown hitting bank earnings
- weak trading quarter

> *"JP Morgan har varit den stora, stabila go-to-banken för oss under många år"*

---

### 🟡 NWG — NatWest | **HOLD** (Weak)

**Sentiment**: Neutral | **Time Horizon**: MT  
**Confidence**: 50%

Guest trimmed NatWest as part of the rotation out of banks into insurance.

#### Reasoning

The guest sold part of the NatWest position because a narrowing rate spread and fading cyclical momentum make banks less attractive. He prefers other European banks over the Nordic ones on valuation. The position has been reduced but apparently not sold out.

#### Sell Triggers

- narrowing net interest margin
- weaker European economy

> *"Vi har sålt både i J.M. Morgan och i våra Nat West."*

---

### 🟠 ROG — Roche | **WATCH** (Weak)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: MT  
**Confidence**: 50%

Phase 3 success; guest says the improving pipeline suggests the stock may be one to look at going forward.

#### Reasoning

The guest owned Roche 4-5 years ago and exited when its research pipeline struggled. The positive Phase 3 cancer result and a better-looking pipeline make it a candidate to revisit, but he owns J&J instead for now.

#### Sell Triggers

- pipeline setbacks
- further trial failures

> *"det verkar nu bli bättre igen vilket talar för att aktien kanske är nåt vi ska titta på framöver"*

---

### 🟡 JNJ — Johnson & Johnson | **HOLD** (Weak)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: LT  
**Confidence**: 50%

Guest's chosen pharma holding instead of Roche.

#### Reasoning

The guest holds J&J as his fund's pharma exposure. Nothing more was said about the thesis beyond it being the preferred choice over Roche for now.

#### Sell Triggers

- switch to Roche if its pipeline keeps improving

> *"vi har valt att äga amerikanska J&amp,J som vårt innehav inom den delen"*

---

### 🟡 CF — CF Industries | **HOLD** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: MT  
**Confidence**: 65%

Owned as a hedge against rising oil and input prices; has performed very well.

#### Reasoning

ESG rules stop the fund from owning energy stocks, so the guest gets indirect exposure to high oil prices through companies that earn spreads on rising input costs and can pass them on. He says these investments have done very well.

#### Sell Triggers

- oil and input prices fall back
- end of the Iran/Hormuz disruption

> *"De investeringarna har gått väldigt bra. Vi äger CF Industries"*

---

### 🟡 ADM — Archer Daniels Midland | **HOLD** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: MT  
**Confidence**: 60%

Owned as a food input-price spread play; has performed well.

#### Reasoning

Same thesis as CF Industries: a company that benefits from rising input prices and can raise its own prices, used as the fund's oil-price hedge in place of energy stocks.

#### Sell Triggers

- commodity prices fall back
- margin squeeze

> *"ett bolag som heter Archer Midland Daniels"*

---

### ⛔ VOLCAR-B — Volvo Cars | **AVOID** (Weak)

**Sentiment**: Negative | **Time Horizon**: MT  
**Confidence**: 50%

Guest has chosen not to own autos because of Chinese competition and rising rates. EFN analyst sees recovery potential if volumes scale.

#### Reasoning

The guest confirms he is staying out of the auto sector. Chinese EVs and plug-in hybrids are flooding Europe, carmakers carry both combustion and electric programmes, and rising rates delay consumer car purchases. Volvo Cars is down about 40% YTD and is one of the most shorted Stockholm stocks. The EFN analyst sees upside if 13 new models can scale volumes at acceptable profitability, and the stock rose ~3% on the CMD.

#### Sell Triggers

- EU restrictions on Chinese EV imports
- successful volume ramp at acceptable margins
- better delivery of the new electric model

> *"Det här är ett bett som ni valt att inte ta. Absolut."*

---

### 🟠 NEWA-B — New Wave | **WATCH** (Weak)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: ST  
**Confidence**: 40%

CEO Torsten Jansson bought shares for nearly 30 MSEK; stock up ~5%.

#### Reasoning

A large insider purchase by the CEO and main owner is a positive signal. The hosts reported it only as news, with no view of their own on the stock.

#### Sell Triggers

- insider selling
- weak next report

> *"vd Torsten Jansson köpte aktier för närmare 30&nbsppkr"*

---

### 🟠 FRO — Frontline | **WATCH** (Weak)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: ST  
**Confidence**: 40%

VLCC rates ~700k USD/day vs 24k break-even, but CEO says it's very cyclical and the rates can't last.

#### Reasoning

Earnings are extraordinary: rates of 700k to 1m USD/day against a cash break-even of about 24k, a structurally tight market and the Hormuz/Iran conflict. But the CEO says the level isn't sustainable, depends on Middle East tensions, and the stock is very volatile after rising 130% YTD. Timing an exit is hard.

#### Sell Triggers

- Middle East tensions ease
- VLCC rates normalise
- Hormuz reopens fully

> *"Du har sagt att man inte ska äga Frontline om man vill sova gott. Det stämmer."*

---
